criteria.text: New tool `rhythm_update_live_artifact_sharing` registered alongside the five existing live-artifact tools in apps/mcp_server/src/tools/liveArtifacts.ts (registerLiveArtifactTools). Operates on EXISTING artifacts only.

Inputs: artifact id; visibility (private | shared | organization); collaborators as human-readable names/emails. Resolve collaborators to workspace user IDs via the hosted API GET /users; exact email match wins, else unambiguous name/email substring match. Ambiguous or unknown identity → error listing candidates, NO mutation performed.

Mutations go through the existing owner-authorized hosted routes: PATCH /live-artifacts/:id for visibility; POST/DELETE /live-artifacts/:id/collaborators for membership diff (fetch current via GET collaborators, apply minimal add/remove diff). Authorization stays server-side — a non-owner actor gets the API's 403 passed through as a clear tool error.
criteria.reason: 2026-08-10: focused HTTP route test passes: owner add → DELETE numeric path parameter returns 204 → GET collaborators is empty; non-numeric path parameter returns 400.

criteria.text: The tool is classified exactly like the existing mutating live-artifact tools (external/outbound action requiring normal approval) — match how update-state/update-bundle are classified in the security boundary. It must NOT be auto-approved reading.
Output never includes raw filesystem paths, tokens/credentials, or any user-management capability beyond this artifact's collaborator list. Returned collaborator info: display name + email only.

Tool count: PR #1338 says 90 tools currently. Registration goes to 91 — update apps/mcp_server/src/__tests__/mcp_capabilities_and_tool_registration.test.ts and any doc/config in apps/mcp_server that asserts the count. Note the count change in your run note (the PR description update is handled by the orchestrator).

Unit + negative tests in apps/mcp_server/src/tools/__tests__/: happy path visibility+collaborators, ambiguous name rejection, unknown user rejection, non-owner 403 passthrough, no-op diff. Follow the existing liveArtifacts.test.ts / .negative.test.ts patterns.

Live behavioral evidence (backend gate): extend the existing env-gated live e2e (apps/api_server/src/__tests__/live_artifacts_mcp_live_e2e.test.ts, RHYTHM_LIVE_E2E=1) with: owner shares artifact with user B by email via the new tool → B can GET the artifact; revoke B → B loses access (403/404). Run it against the isolated sandbox: from the worktree, tools/dev/sandbox.sh up (API :4098), run the test, tools/dev/sandbox.sh down. NEVER hand-start api_server or the engine; the live engine on :4096 must stay untouched. Record exact command + output in the run note.
criteria.reason: 2026-08-10: rebuilt isolated :4098/:4097 sandbox, then the exact env-gated E2E passed (1 file / 1 test, 12.20s). It proves denied post-taint revoke retains 200 access; exact sharing approval then succeeds without a Rhythm API error, removes the collaborator grant row (count 0), and collaborator GET returns 404.

criteria.text: The trusted approval verifier binds `live-artifact.sharing.update` only to `rhythm_update_live_artifact_sharing`; a state-update signed envelope is rejected for a sharing approval.

not_tested: Signed human-approval decision (PATCH /agent-approvals/:id). The sandbox is configured with the desktop HUMAN_APPROVAL_PUBLIC_KEY / capability digest only — the P-256 private half and the raw capability live in the desktop Keychain, so no sandbox test can produce a valid signature. The live test drives the real request-approval path and then flips that one server-minted pending row to approved to stand in for the human tap; every binding property (session, agent, action, canonical payload digest, taint, single-use consumption) is still enforced by the real server. The signature ceremony itself is covered by human_approval_signature.test.ts and issue_1175_adversarial_live.test.ts.
